anchor: Table of specific commitments in Keep Britain Working: a national growth opportunity, September 2026 (GOV.UK, updated 9 October 2026)
notes: PROPOSED by RFC 0003, profile-scoped (owhs-uk-measures). The source describes these as commitments being tested and as early examples, not firm proposals. 'sourceText' quotes the published table. 'timer' is the published time limit where one is given; 'counting' is an OWHS proposal wherever the source does not say how to count. Record the dates; compute the status. If the counting rule changes, nothing needs collecting again.

values.sourceText: A work and health conversation offered within 8 weeks of joining.
values.counting: PROPOSED: 56 calendar days from the employment start date

values.sourceText: A conversation within 5 working days of an issue being raised
values.trigger: date the worker or manager raised the issue
values.counting: PROPOSED: working days are Monday to Friday excluding public holidays in the worker's UK nation; the day the issue is raised is day zero

values.sourceText: a stay-in-work plan with named actions, owners and review points
values.counting: no time limit published; dates recorded only

values.sourceText: Adjustments agreed promptly and put in place as quickly as practicable.
values.trigger: date the adjustment was requested or recommended
values.counting: no time limit published; dates recorded only

values.sourceText: Adjustments agreed promptly and put in place as quickly as practicable.
values.completion: date the adjustment was in place (ReasonableAdjustment.startDate)
values.counting: no time limit published; dates recorded only

values.sourceText: Contact on day one of absence where possible, and no later than day 3.
values.completion: date of first contact between employer and worker
values.counting: PROPOSED: calendar days, counting the first day of absence as day one, so day 3 is startDate plus 2 days. The source does not say whether days are calendar or working days.

values.sourceText: co-created for any absence and particularly those likely to pass 4 weeks or linked to underlying conditions
values.completion: date the return-to-work plan was agreed with the worker
values.counting: PROPOSED: for any absence that reaches 28 calendar days, a plan agreed on or before day 28. The source gives no deadline for the plan and 'likely to pass' is a judgement that cannot be recorded as a date.

values.sourceText: with provision engaged within ten working days where needed
values.trigger: date the need for provision was recorded
values.completion: date the provider was engaged (OHEpisode.referralDate where the provision is occupational health)
values.counting: PROPOSED: working days as for issue-conversation. The source does not say what starts the clock.

values.sourceText: Regular touchpoints established with agreement of the employee.
values.completion: date a contact pattern was agreed with the worker
values.counting: no time limit published; dates recorded only

values.sourceText: Sustained return measured at 6 months, not day one.
values.completion: date the 26-week status was recorded (ReturnToWorkOutcome.sustainedAt, checkpointWeeks 26)
values.counting: PROPOSED: 26 weeks (182 calendar days) after rtwDate, matching the existing OWHS recommended checkpoint
